title: Broad current-reality change scan — trends are search signals, not opportunity verdicts
purpose: Return to broad current Xuzhou/Jiangsu reality changes after mechanism-specific scans 009–013 produced zero retained candidates. Test whether any current state change creates bilateral action plus a narrow post-incumbent missing edge suitable for a low-permission Rooter control plane.
scan_rule: NEW INTERNATIONAL FLOW != LOW-PERMISSION ROOTER WEDGE
RESOURCE REDEPLOYMENT != PRIVATE ROUTING OPPORTUNITY when the bridge is already institutionalized or permission-heavy

patterns_tested.reality_change: Jiangsu SMEs increasingly serve small-batch, high-frequency, diverse, short-cycle export orders.
patterns_tested.missing_edge: NO DISTINCT POST-INCUMBENT ROOTER GAP OBSERVED

patterns_tested.pattern: Xuzhou plant-based cat-litter export compliance / country-specific standards
patterns_tested.reality_change: Xuzhou plant-based cat litter exports now reach dozens of countries and face country-specific standards and compliance requirements.

reality_change: Current Jiangsu manufacturers in batteries, semiconductors, transformers and other categories report full-load production or long forward order books.
Global transformer buyers are physically stationed at factories for acceptance and to lock future capacity.
counterevidence: High-value output is highly customized and qualification-heavy.
OEM direct sales, supply-chain clusters and buyer factory presence already own the relationship.
Capacity pressure is handled through expansion, internal scheduling, supplier ecosystems and direct commercial negotiation.
patterns_tested.rooter_risk: Would become procurement agent / project coordinator / capacity broker in a highly qualified nonstandard market.

patterns_tested.reality_change: A Suzhou industrial-park enterprise at full load faced an order-delivery power shortage and the park coordinated connection from nearby idle factory capacity.
why_not_candidate: Electrical connection is safety-, asset- and permission-heavy.
Jiangsu has already institutionalized flexible load participation through rapid-response load markets and explicitly recognizes virtual-power-plant/load-aggregator participation.
The commercial control plane is therefore already moving into a regulated utility/aggregator market.

patterns_tested.pattern: global after-sales repair orders returning to Jiangsu
patterns_tested.reality_change: Global repair/calibration/replacement demand for medical, electronics and precision equipment is increasing and more work is returning to Jiangsu.

reality_change: Xuzhou aging is high and rural aging is materially higher than urban areas.
Families report real travel/care burden for elderly medical needs.

patterns_tested.reality_change: Urban consumers pay for time-saving proxy services such as pet care and errands.
patterns_tested.incumbent_evidence: Xuzhou media reports more than 3000 relevant platform shops, top merchants with thousands of orders and high review rates.
patterns_tested.missing_edge: NONE OBSERVED AT GENERIC ROUTING LAYER

patterns_tested.pattern: idle preschool/medical/public-space repurposing toward elder care
patterns_tested.reality_change: Falling child population and rising elderly demand are pushing some Jiangsu facilities toward elder-care reuse.
why_not_candidate: asset conversion, healthcare and elder-care operation are permission-heavy
current conversions are being organized by public/institutional operators
no low-capital repeatable Rooter transaction unit is observed

material_learning: Broad state changes are valuable search signals but repeatedly fail after current vertical/institutional routes are considered.
Strong bilateral pressure often attracts rapid incumbent scope expansion, institutional coordination or regulated aggregation.
A Rooter candidate must therefore be observed after those adaptations, not inferred from the original pressure.
Household and public-service scarcity is not automatically a private low-permission platform opportunity.
scan_conclusion.current_best_next_truth: Fresh Scan 015 should stop starting from trends. Search for explicit recent failed or repeatedly costly transactions after an incumbent channel already exists: repeated failed procurement, repeated outsourcing rejection, repeated cross-city workaround, failed acceptance, or transactions that actors are visibly retrying. Prefer private/low-permission cases and avoid using public-tender failure alone as an opportunity.
